name: OpenClaw
vibe_summary: The canonical self-hosted AI assistant gateway that connects your chat channels to agentic models on your own devices. Massive community, rapid release cadence, and a sprawling skills/plugin ecosystem make it the reference implementation everything else is compared against.
best_for: Users wanting one assistant across WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, and more
Self-hosters who want local-first control with optional cloud models
Teams sharing a trusted gateway deployment
Power users building custom skills and automations
avoid_if: You want a zero-maintenance managed SaaS assistant
You are uncomfortable granting an agent shell and device access
You need a lightweight embedded or edge runtime
You are wary of fast-moving releases occasionally breaking setups
openclaw_advantages: This is the reference project: largest community, docs, and skill registry
Broadest channel support (WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, Teams, and more)
Native companion apps on iOS, Android, macOS, Linux, Windows
Single gateway scales from personal laptop to trusted team deployment
openclaw_disadvantages: Node.js runtime footprint is heavier than Rust/Go alternatives
Broad device and shell access raises the security stakes of misconfiguration
Rapid release cadence has caused update regressions for some users
Feature breadth can be overwhelming for minimal single-purpose setups

overview_markdown:
OpenClaw is the original open-source, self-hosted AI assistant gateway: a single Node.js/TypeScript process that runs on your own hardware and bridges the messaging channels you already use — WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Slack, Discord, iMessage, Teams, and more — to agentic AI models. Its core architectural stance is 'trusted gateway, untrusted execution, deterministic policy': the gateway holds credentials and channel connections, while tool execution and skills run under configurable policy, scaling from a personal laptop assistant to a shared team deployment with configuration as the only difference.

The ecosystem around it is a major differentiator: the ClawHub skill registry (with 5,400+ community skills), native companion apps for iOS/Android/desktop, a Control UI dashboard, and support for both cloud models and local models via Ollama. Recent commits show heavy investment in reliability and performance — worker spawn fixes, plugin catalog lookup optimization, and conversation lifecycle correctness — alongside a very fast release cadence (v2026.9.2 at time of analysis).

Compared to clones and alternatives, OpenClaw trades footprint for breadth: it is heavier than minimal Rust/Go agents and its deep device/shell access demands careful security configuration, but no alternative matches its channel coverage, community size (~389k stars), or plugin ecosystem. Community sentiment is broadly positive but not uncritical — Reddit threads document update regressions and debates about its long-term direction, which is typical for a project moving this fast.
